notes: Fiscal year ended August 30, 2026 (Costco's 52-week fiscal 2026). Financial figures are from the FY2026 Form 10-K (accession 0000909832-26-000093, filed October 7, 2026) and match SEC XBRL. Ownership is from the proxy for the January 2026 annual meeting (DEF 14A filed December 4, 2025, accession 0000909832-25-000159), the latest proxy on file at November 24, 2026; the proxy for the January 2027 meeting had not yet been filed, so ownership is as of November 7, 2025, before fiscal 2026 ended. LEADER: James Sinegal, co-founder and former CEO, is not a director or named executive officer and does not appear in either ownership table (5% holders, or directors and officers), so his holding, if any, is not reported. HOLDERS: both 5% rows are based on Form 13F-HR filings made November 7 and November 12, 2025; the proxy gives only the filing dates, so asOf is null. The percentages use 443,957,682 shares outstanding. DIVIDENDS: cash paid of $2,458 million equals dividends declared in fiscal 2026 ($5.54 per share); there was no special dividend in fiscal 2026. BUYBACKS exclude $361 million of tax withholdings on stock-based awards. PLAN: the 10-K mentions an employee stock ownership plan (ESOP) only as a line in the income-tax rate reconciliation and describes no employee stock purchase plan, so plan is null.

taxes.notes: Fiscal year ended August 30, 2026. Taxes: cash paid for income taxes, net of refunds (us-gaap:IncomeTaxesPaidNet), from the new by-jurisdiction schedule in Note 8 (Costco adopted ASU 2023-09 for fiscal 2026); the supplemental cash-flow line 'Income taxes, net' shows the same $2,839 million. R&D not reported as a separate line (retailer).

paidout.notes: 52-week fiscal year ended August 30, 2026 (FY2026 Form 10-K). Revenue includes membership fees (5.907bn). Capex is the single "Additions to property and equipment" line; Costco reports no separate intangibles line. Interest and income taxes paid are inside operating cash flow.

pay.notes: Employees: year-end count for fiscal 2026, including part-time employees (the 10-K says Costco targets at least 50% full-time and also uses seasonal employees). Payroll: the 10-K says compensation and benefits are its largest expense after merchandise but gives no total, so the CEO pay ratio median is used. It comes from the proxy filed December 4, 2025 and covers fiscal 2025 (median identified on June 30, 2025 from about 323,800 full-time, part-time, seasonal and temporary employees; ratio 283:1), a year behind the head count; the proxy for fiscal 2026 was not yet filed.
